problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[1,3]\times [1,3]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{3} \\ {x}^{2}-xy+1\end{aligned}].
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting  at the point $[2,\,2]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration.

| $[$ | {{field-1}} | $-12$ | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | $-8$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  |  |  |

| ${x}_{1}=[$ | $1.9$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-4}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as 

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}-{y}^{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{4}-{y}^{3}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-xy+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-xy+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3} & -3{y}^{2} \\ 2x-y & -x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3} & -3{y}^{2} \\ 2x-y & -x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{3} \\ {x}^{2}-xy+1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}4{x}^{3} & -3{y}^{2} \\ 2x-y & -x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-{y}^{3} \\ {x}^{2}-xy+1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}4(2)^{3} & -3(2)^{2} \\ 2(2)-2 & -2\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}{2}^{4}-{2}^{3} \\ {2}^{2}-(2)(2)+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}32 & -12 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}-0.1 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}-0.1 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-0.1 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.9 \\ 2.4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
